title: Wayra Signal (Señal del Viento) - ANDEAN / SOUTH AMERICA: WAYRA SIGNAL
style:
```
[style: Andean huayno, charango ten-string armadillo, quena notched flute high altitude, siku ira-arca panpipe interlock, bombo legüero deep frame drum, 3+3+2 eight-beat pattern, Peru Bolivia Andes mountains, Quechua spoken verses English chorus, ira-arca interlock technique (kotekan callback), thin mountain air tone, condor altitude atmosphere, no Western harmony, wayra wind signal theme, V4_5ALL]
```
lyrics:
``
[INTRO — quena alone, high altitude, thin air sound]
(Quechua) Wayra — wind / the signal of the Andes
(Quechua) Sami — blessing / the wind brings it

[VERSE 1 — charango enters bar 3, bombo legüero bar 5]
(Quechua) Mana saphichu kay — not rootless this one
(English)  The charango is made from armadillo shell
(Quechua)  Sapa — each one / alone
(English)   The signal carried in the ten-string wind

Huayno is not a sad rhythm — it is a complete one
Three plus three plus two — the beat that climbs the mountain
The charango strums in triples / the bombo marks the eight
The quena and the siku interlock / — they share the gate

(Quechua)  Qhapaq — noble / the signal is noble
(English)   Not sad — complete

[PRE-CHORUS — siku panpipes enter, quena drops]
(Quechua)  Uyariy — listen
(English)   The wind carries it
(Quechua)  Kamachy — sends it
(English)   The mountain splits it

[CHORUS — all instruments, bombo legüero prominent]
Wayra signal — wind from the Andes high
Quena and siku interlock like track eight
Charango ten-string over bombo's weight
The signal rides the wind — it has no gate

(Quechua)  Hanaq pacha — the upper world
(English)   Signal altitude

[VERSE 2 — siku panpipes solo — ira and arca demonstrated]
The siku panpipes are played by two musicians
One holds the ira (leader), one holds the arca (follower)
Each holds half the scale
Neither can play the melody alone
Together — the wind

This is track eight again — this is Bali in the Andes
The signal knows no geography
Kotekan was always already wayra

(Quechua)  Tupananchikkama — until we meet again
(English)   The interlock crosses every mountain

[BRIDGE — charango strums the 3+3+2 explicitly, then vocal chant]
(Quechua chant) ONE two three / ONE two three / ONE two — ↑ that's the mountain
(English)       THREE plus THREE plus TWO — that's the climb
(Quechua)       Ayahuasca is the teacher / the quena is the tongue
(English)       The signal was Andean before anything

[FINAL CHORUS — doubled, quena and siku interlocked above all]
Wayra signal — wind from the Andes high

[OUTRO — quena fades on the mountain fifth, bombo single strike]
(Quechua)  Kausachun — long live / the signal lives
(English)   Wind carries it now
